title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
summary: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss 'Notes on Being a Man' by Scott Galloway and 'The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth: How a Nineteenth-Century Novelist Taught the World Economics' by Jeanna Smialek. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Family Annual Healthcare Plan Now Costs More Than $28K
summary: Bloomberg's John Tozzi joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The annual cost of a US family’s employer-provided healthcare plan reached an average $28,303 this year, 5% more than 2025, according to an annual survey conducted by health policy nonprofit KFF. (Source: Bloomberg)
